02

Three Gaps in Energy Estates

I

The Automation Now Reaches Equipment That Can Hurt People.

Models that began by advising operators now send instructions to plant. Each step was probably approved by a competent engineer. Can you point to the place where advice turned into action?

II

A Segmentation Diagram Is a Claim, Not Evidence.

The design says the boundary holds. The traffic is the only thing that can confirm it. When was the boundary last tested by watching what actually crosses it?

III

The Evidence Exists, but Not in a Form Anyone Can Audit.

Most estates are more secure than they can demonstrate. If a regulator asked for proof that a control operates, would you be assembling it or retrieving it?

04

Common Questions

What does a control evidence review examine at a utility?

The tested behavior of the IT/OT boundary, where office systems meet operational technology: what a compromised credential or management interface can actually reach, compared against the documented design. A full segmentation redesign is covered by our Infrastructure Design Review.

Is IEC 62443 mandatory in the GCC?

It is the sector standard rather than a dated national obligation. It is usually the framework a safety case, the documented argument that a plant is safe to operate, is written against.

Does the UAE encryption policy apply to utility operators?

The National Encryption Policy applies across the estate, and the migration plan it requires rests on a cryptographic inventory.

Do you provide OT monitoring or incident response?

Yes, through our Managed Detection & Response service: 24/7 monitoring and response on an annual term, with onboarding in 30 to 45 days. Which operational segments it covers is agreed at scoping with the owner of your safety case.

Can an assessment run without touching production systems?

Yes. Scope is agreed at the outset, and observation stays passive unless you explicitly authorize otherwise.
